## About these materials

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Citation statement
Please cite these materials as: Gupta, R., Meier, L., & Middleton, L. S. (2026). *FAIR Research Data Management: A hands-on, actionable workshop for researchers* [Quarto slides]. [LMU Open Science Center](https://www.osc.lmu.de/). [https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-materials/fair-data](https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-materials/fair-data)
:::

**Welcome!** This workshop is intended to help learners **bridge the gap** between knowing they *should* share their research data and feeling confident to actually do it. Learners will see which parts of the **FAIR principles** (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) are **their responsibility** and which are handled by repositories and tools. The session then turns these principles into **practical skills** for **organizing**, **documenting**, and **sharing** research data, from folder structures, file naming and file formats to data dictionaries, READMEs and metadata. Through short hands-on activities, learners **discover the standards** their field already uses, **pick a repository** and **choose a license** for their own data. The session takes about **105 minutes** and includes polls, a quiz and two worksheet activities.

### Who are these materials for?

- **Educators** in higher education with or without familiarity with open research planning to **teach open research** to **novices**
- **Self-learners** with no or limited familiarity with open research planning to **develop and build** up on their open research skills

### Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;">
| Prerequisite   |  Description  | Link/Where to find it   |
|------------|------------|------------|
| UNESCO Recommendations on Open Science | For a first overview of Open Research, particularly pp 6-19 | [Download here](https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000379949) |
| Laptop with internet access | Needed for the toolkit and repository activities | |
</div>

### Learning objectives

At the end of this session, you or your learners will be able to ...

- **Distinguish** the parts of FAIR you should and should *not* worry about
- **Apply** practical skills for organizing, documenting, and sharing research data
- **Find and adopt** the standards your field already uses
- **Commit** to one concrete next step to take within the next month
